title: How this lesson works
text: Before you start · your group ≈ 2 min How this lesson works Slideshow lead Reads each slide aloud and moves the deck forward. Whiteboard scribe Holds the dry erase marker and works problems at the whiteboard. Timekeeper · support Starts each timer and keeps the group on pace. Checker · support Asks "How do we know?" before anyone presses Show answer. Explicit instruction Read it together. Then one person restates it in their own words. Check your understanding Solve alone, compare answers, agree — then press Show answer. Group tasks Start the timer. Everyone contributes before you move on. Exit ticket On your own. Submit it with this lesson's assignment. Day 5 · Predicting Position Antocci Physics · 02 / 30 2 students: lead + timekeeper, scribe + checker. 3 students: third person takes both support duties. Roles rotate at each discussion. Everyone submits their own work.

title: Today's learning target

title: The asteroid thread

title: Flip the definition
text: Recap ≈ 5 min Flip the definition Velocity v = Δx ÷ Δt So displacement Δx = v × Δt If velocity stays constant, we can predict where it will be later. Day 5 · Predicting Position Antocci Physics · 05 / 30

title: Start somewhere, then move
text: See it → describe it Target R3 Start somewhere, then move The cart starts at 2 m. It moves +2 m each second. The starting position matters At 0 s the position is already 2 m. Day 5 · Predicting Position Antocci Physics · 06 / 30

title: Units before multiplication
text: Check your understanding Target R3 Units before multiplication A train travels at 40 m/s for 2 hours. Find its displacement if velocity stays constant. Solve alone · compare as a group · then check. Your turn Work it out on paper. Then press Show answer to check. Day 5 · Predicting Position Antocci Physics · 07 / 30

title: A prediction can be a range
text: See it → describe it Target R3 A prediction can be a range Our central prediction is 10 m. “10 ± 2 m” means from 8 to 12 m. Not one perfectly known point The full range is 4 m wide. It is not a probability. Day 5 · Predicting Position Antocci Physics · 08 / 30

title: Position includes the starting point
text: Explicit instruction Target R3 Position includes the starting point x f = x 0 + v x t For constant velocity, displacement is vₓt. The initial position can be nonzero. In two dimensions, also use y f = y 0 + v y t. Day 5 · Predicting Position Antocci Physics · 09 / 30

title: Choose the axes before calculating
text: 2026-XJ · The Window · Graphic novel, page 17 Choose the axes before calculating The classroom model starts at positive 120 million kilometers on the x axis with Earth at the origin. Toward-Earth motion has negative x velocity. Maz and Nadia explain that changing axes changes signs, not the motion. Day 5 uses the novel’s fixed axes: +x points toward the starting location; +y is sideways. Why is toward-Earth velocity negative on these axes? Part 1 · Check the start, change and axes · Write your own answer in Work. Fictional story · Original artwork · Day 5

title: What we know
text: The prediction problem ≈ 20 min What we know Quantity Value Current position (+1.2 × 10⁸ km, 0) x velocity · toward Earth −8,210 m/s = −8.210 km/s y velocity · sideways +2,200 m/s = +2.200 km/s Time forward 6 months ≈ 1.6 × 10⁷ s Day 5 · Predicting Position Antocci Physics · 11 / 30

title: Predict the new position
text: Calculate ≈ 20 min Predict the new position 01 Make the units match — m or km, not both. 02 Find the displacement in each direction: Δx = v × Δt. 03 Add each displacement to the current position. 04 Check the exponent: does the size make sense? Work Time Day 5 · Predicting Position Antocci Physics · 12 / 30

title: Step 1: find the change
text: I do · one operation Target R3 Work Step 1: find the change Velocity: +2 m/s. Time: 3 s. Change = 2 × 3 = +6 m One change per second Add three equal changes. Day 5 · Predicting Position Antocci Physics · 13 / 30

title: A local prediction
text: Check your understanding Target R3 Work A local prediction A cart starts at x₀ = 12 m and moves at −2 m/s for 4 s. Find displacement and final position. title: Step 2: add the starting position
text: I do · one operation Target R3 Work Step 2: add the starting position Start at 2 m. Move +6 m. Final position = 2 + 6 = 8 m Follow the cart Displacement is +6 m; final position is 8 m. Day 5 · Predicting Position Antocci Physics · 15 / 30

title: One model's prediction
text: Compare ≈ 15 min One model's prediction Start (1.2 × 10⁸ km, 0) Velocity (−8.210, +2.200) km/s After 1.6 × 10⁷ s (−1.14 × 10⁷, 3.52 × 10⁷) km From Earth ≈ 3.70 × 10⁷ km Earth at the origin; +x toward the asteroid's start. A constant-velocity model — not an orbit. Day 5 · Predicting Position Antocci Physics · 16 / 30

title: A negative coordinate is not a collision
text: 2026-XJ · The Window · Graphic novel, page 18 A negative coordinate is not a collision Eli asks whether negative x means a collision. Maz points to the positive y coordinate. The straight model path starts at 120 million kilometers on x and ends at negative 11.36 million x and positive 35.20 million y, passing above Earth. Use both coordinates to describe the endpoint. The six-month separation is about 37 million km. Why is this endpoint distance different from closest approach? Part 2 · Check the two-dimensional prediction · Write your own answer in Work. Fictional story · Original artwork · Day 5

title: How sure are we?
text: Critical question ≈ 15 min How sure are we? Each coordinate: starting position ±50,000 km; velocity component ±0.200 km/s. Treat elapsed time as exact. Day 5 · Predicting Position Antocci Physics · 18 / 30

title: Sketch the window
text: Uncertainty ≈ 15 min Sketch the window 01 For each coordinate, add the initial bound to the velocity bound × time. 02 Sketch the "window" of possible locations. 03 Which effects does this window leave out? Work Time Day 5 · Predicting Position Antocci Physics · 19 / 30

title: Coordinates for the asteroid model
text: Fictional model assumptions Target R3 Work Coordinates for the asteroid model Put Earth at (0, 0) and the asteroid initially at (+1.2 × 10⁸ km, 0). Define +x toward the initial asteroid location and +y sideways. Use vₓ = −8.210 km/s and vᵧ = +2.200 km/s. The direction is 15° from −x toward +y. Let six months mean 1.6 × 10⁷ s in this task. Freeze Earth at the origin and hold velocity constant. These are deliberate simplifications. Day 5 · Predicting Position Antocci Physics · 20 / 30

title: Predict together
text: Try it as a group Target R3 Work Predict together Start at 1 m. Velocity is +3 m/s. Time is 2 s. Find change first. Then final position. Solve alone · compare as a group · then check. Follow the cart The first second adds 3 m. Day 5 · Predicting Position Antocci Physics · 21 / 30

title: Worked two-dimensional prediction
text: Explicit instruction Target R3 Work Worked two-dimensional prediction v x ≈ −8.210 km/s, v y ≈ 2.200 km/s x f = +1.20 × 10⁸ − 8.210(1.6 × 10⁷) x f ≈ −1.14 × 10⁷ km and y f ≈ +3.52 × 10⁷ km . Distance from the fixed origin ≈ √(x f ² + y f ²) ≈ 3.70 × 10⁷ km . Day 5 · Predicting Position Antocci Physics · 22 / 30

title: Read a measurement range
text: Try it as a group Target R3 Work Read a measurement range A prediction is 6 ± 1 m. Name the lowest and highest predicted positions. Solve alone · compare as a group · then check. A path through the problem 01 Below the center Subtract 1. 02 Above the center Add 1. Read one step at a time. Day 5 · Predicting Position Antocci Physics · 23 / 30

title: The window is part of the answer
text: 2026-XJ · The Window · Graphic novel, page 19 The window is part of the answer Eli and Maz discuss measurement limits. A rectangle around the predicted endpoint extends 3.25 million kilometers from the center in each coordinate. It represents bounds on x and y, not an impact probability. 50,000 + 0.200 × 16,000,000 = 3,250,000 km in each coordinate. What is the full width? What does this window leave out? Part 3 · Defend the window and its limits · Write your own answer in Work. Fictional story · Original artwork · Day 5

title: The scenario is fiction. The methods are real.

title: Position and displacement are different vectors
text: Check your understanding Target R3 Position and displacement are different vectors The model travels about 1.36 × 10⁸ km in six months. Why is that different from the final 3.70 × 10⁷ km separation from Earth? Solve alone · compare as a group · then check. Your turn Work it out on paper. Then press Show answer to check. Day 5 · Predicting Position Antocci Physics · 26 / 30

title: Why does more time matter?
text: Explain before calculating Target R3 Why does more time matter? A small uncertainty in velocity adds uncertainty each second. A longer prediction usually spreads farther out. Same uncertain motion, more time Central Lower bound Upper bound The shaded region is a measurement bound, not a probability. Day 5 · Predicting Position Antocci Physics · 27 / 30

title: Test what the model leaves out
text: 2026-XJ · The Window · Graphic novel, page 20 Test what the model leaves out Mr. Antocci says the window covers only the measurement limits included. Nadia asks about the Sun’s gravity. Maz circles constant velocity because gravity changes velocity and the straight-line model leaves it out. Measurement bounds do not automatically include missing physics. What observation would test constant velocity, and what model change would address gravity? Part 3 · Defend the window and its limits · Write your own answer in Work. Fictional story · Original artwork · Day 5
